metadata.description: GitHub Actions workflow deploying to Azure, triggered by push and workflow_dispatch events.

extras.workflow_content:
name: Deploy to Azure

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

env:
  AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME: openai-cs-agents-backend
  AZURE_WEBAPP_PACKAGE_PATH: './python-backend'
  PYTHON_VERSION: '3.11'
  NODE_VERSION: '20'
  RESOURCE_GROUP: openai-cs-agents-demo-rg
  LOCATION: eastus2
  APP_SERVICE_PLAN: openai-cs-agents-plan
  STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME: openai-cs-agents-frontend

jobs:
  build-and-deploy-backend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ env.PYTHON_VERSION }}

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: ./python-backend
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -r requirements.txt

      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Create Resource Group (if not exists)
        run: |
          az group create --name ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} --location ${{ env.LOCATION }} || true

      - name: Create App Service Plan (Free Tier)
        run: |
          az appservice plan create \
            --name ${{ env.APP_SERVICE_PLAN }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --sku F1 \
            --is-linux || true

      - name: Create Web App
        run: |
          az webapp create \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --plan ${{ env.APP_SERVICE_PLAN }} \
            --runtime "PYTHON:3.11" || true

      - name: Configure App Settings
        run: |
          az webapp config appsettings set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --settings \
              OPENAI_API_KEY="${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}" \
              SCM_DO_BUILD_DURING_DEPLOYMENT=true \
              WEBSITES_PORT=8000

      - name: Configure startup command
        run: |
          az webapp config set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --startup-file "gunicorn -w 2 -k uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker api:app --bind 0.0.0.0:8000"

      - name: Deploy to Azure Web App
        uses: azure/webapps-deploy@v3
        with:
          app-name: ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }}
          package: ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_PACKAGE_PATH }}

      - name: Output Backend URL
        id: backend-url
        run: |
          BACKEND_URL="https://${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }}.azurewebsites.net"
          echo "BACKEND_URL=$BACKEND_URL" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "Backend deployed to: $BACKEND_URL"

    outputs:
      backend_url: ${{ steps.backend-url.outputs.BACKEND_URL }}

  build-and-deploy-frontend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: build-and-deploy-backend
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}

      - name: Install pnpm
        run: npm install -g pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: ./ui
        run: pnpm install

      - name: Build frontend
        working-directory: ./ui
        run: pnpm run build
        env:
          NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE: ${{ needs.build-and-deploy-backend.outputs.backend_url }}

      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Create Static Web App (if not exists)
        run: |
          az staticwebapp create \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --location ${{ env.LOCATION }} \
            --sku Free || true

      - name: Get Static Web App deployment token
        id: swa-token
        run: |
          TOKEN=$(az staticwebapp secrets list \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "properties.apiKey" -o tsv)
          echo "::add-mask::$TOKEN"
          echo "DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN=$TOKEN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Deploy to Azure Static Web Apps
        uses: Azure/static-web-apps-deploy@v1
        with:
          azure_static_web_apps_api_token: ${{ steps.swa-token.outputs.DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN }}
          repo_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          action: "upload"
          app_location: "./ui/out"
          output_location: ""
          skip_app_build: true

      - name: Output Frontend URL
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL=$(az staticwebapp show \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "defaultHostname" -o tsv)
          echo "Frontend deployed to: https://$FRONTEND_URL"

  configure-cors:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [build-and-deploy-backend, build-and-deploy-frontend]
    
    steps:
      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Get Static Web App URL
        id: frontend-url
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL=$(az staticwebapp show \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "defaultHostname" -o tsv)
          echo "FRONTEND_URL=https://$FRONTEND_URL" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Configure CORS on Backend
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL="${{ steps.frontend-url.outputs.FRONTEND_URL }}"
          # Pass ALLOWED_ORIGINS to FastAPI's CORSMiddleware via app setting.
          # Do NOT use `az webapp cors add` together with FastAPI's own CORSMiddleware —
          # both would add Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers, causing duplicate-header
          # rejections in browsers.  FastAPI's middleware is the single source of truth.
          az webapp config appsettings set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --settings ALLOWED_ORIGINS="$FRONTEND_URL,http://localhost:3250,http://localhost:3000"
          # Clear any previously-added Azure-level CORS origins to avoid conflicts.
          az webapp cors remove \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --allowed-origins "*" || true

      - name: Summary
        run: |
          echo "=== Deployment Complete ==="
          echo "Backend URL: ${{ needs.build-and-deploy-backend.outputs.backend_url }}"
          echo "Frontend URL: ${{ steps.frontend-url.outputs.FRONTEND_URL }}"

summary.use_case: This system implements an agentic AI workflow for customer service, serving users with FAQ question answering and request triage/routing. It features five specialized GPT-4 agents (Cancellation, FAQ, Flight Status, Seat Booking, Triage) with jailbreak and relevance guardrails, backed by a Sqlite datastore and FastAPI endpoints with Bearer authentication. The application supports text-only interactions, with no voice, image, or video modality support.
summary.iac_security_summary:
## Security briefing

### 1) Deployment posture
- **Cloud provider / runtime:** Azure (az group, az webapp, Deploy to Azure)
- **Regions / HA / resilience:** Not evidenced
- **Assessment:** The deployment targets Azure Web Apps via GitHub Actions, but no regions, availability zones, or high-availability configuration are specified.

### 2) Secret management
- **Secret stores:** GitHub Actions secrets (github_actions_secret)
- **Credential handling:** Azure Credentials are referenced as a GitHub Actions secret (${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}), indicating no plaintext exposure in code.
- **Assessment:** Secrets are stored in GitHub Actions, which is appropriate for CI/CD, but the absence of an external vault (e.g., Azure Key Vault) limits rotation and audit capabilities.

### 3) Encryption
- **Encryption at rest:** Not evidenced (encryption_at_rest_coverage: false)
- **Key management:** Not evidenced
- **Assessment:** No encryption-at-rest configuration or key management details are provided; this is a significant gap for an AI application handling sensitive data.

### 4) IAM / least privilege
- **Principals / service accounts:** ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }} (managed_identity)
- **Scope / permissions / trust:** Subscription-level scope; trust principals include "github-actions"; uses managed identity but no role or permission details are specified.
- **Assessment:** The subscription-wide scope of the managed identity violates least privilege; it should be scoped to a resource group or specific resource.

### 5) CI/CD security
- **Runners / triggers:** ubuntu-latest; triggers: push, workflow_dispatch
- **OIDC / credential flow:** OIDC not used (uses_oidc: false); credentials are passed via secrets.
- **Assessment:** Without OIDC, long-lived secrets are used in CI/CD; this increases credential exposure risk and should be replaced with federated identity.

### 6) Container security
- **Images / root user:** Not evidenced
- **Health checks / resource limits:** Not evidenced
- **Assessment:** No container configuration (images, health checks, or resource limits) is present; Gunicorn and Uvicorn suggest containerized Python workloads but lack security hardening.

### 7) Top 3 prioritized actions
1. Replace subscription-scoped managed identity with a resource group or app-level scope and define minimal RBAC roles based on actual service needs.
2. Enable OIDC between GitHub Actions and Azure to eliminate long-lived secrets in CI/CD credentials.
3. Implement encryption at rest (e.g., Azure Storage Service Encryption) for any data stores and document key management (Azure Key Vault or customer-managed keys).

- **Architecture & Flow**: The system uses a **FastAPI** framework exposing endpoints (`Chat`, `Login`, `Me`, `Logout`) – all probably protected by **Bearer Auth** (heuristic, confidence 0.40). User input flows through a **Chat Endpoint**, then likely orchestrated by **OpenAI Agents** (heuristic) which delegates to domain agents: **Triage Agent** → **Flight Status Agent** & **FAQ Agent**. All agents probably call the same set of tools (e.g. `Flight Status Tool`, `Baggage Tool`, `Cancel Flight`) and likely use **gpt-4.1-mini** for decision-making.

- **Guardrails**: Two guardrails (**Relevance Guardrail** and **Jailbreak Guardrail**) are confirmed using gpt-4.1-mini and custom prompt instructions. They *probably* protect all agents (heuristic, confidence 0.40). Notably, no guardrail protects tools directly.

- **Security Observations**:  
  - No risk tags are present on any node in the graph – no `[no-auth-required]` or `[SQL-injectable]` tags were found, meaning no pre-identified concrete security risks are reported here.  
  - If guardrails are bypassed, agents have reach to all tools (including `Cancel Flight`, `Update Seat`, `Display Seat Map`) with no explicit tool-level access controls.  
  - **Sqlite** datastore appears in the graph but with no connections – it is isolated, though its usage context is unknown.
